b: You can correct glaring mistakes. It’s subtle blunders that defeat you.
You proved yourself when they hired you.
Find confidence in your ability to listen, learn, and decide. You never know it all and you never have all the answers.
Remember that your words and actions deeply impact those around you.
There’s almost always more to the story.
People minimize their mistakes and exaggerate their successes.
Flashy people talk about things they’re going to do. Look for real results.
Curiosity, transparency, and candor answer gullibility. Keep exploring. Ask questions before making statements.
Listen to quiet doers before flashy talkers.
Distant deadlines get put on the shelf.
Set short-term goals that allow teams to start again.
It’s better to finish one thing and start another than to chase urgent trivialities.
You need big wins. How you achieve them is what matters.
Big wins are the result of many small wins.
Listen to make others feel heard.
If you aren’t careful, responsibility multiplies misery.
Focus on things you can control.
The fear of mistakes is a mistake.
